title: Historical disciplinary counseling and case-documentation workflow
summary: Repeated structure across 33 restricted individual-warning artifacts shows two dominant historical documentation paths: free-form personnel-file counseling memos and a standardized Employee Warning Notice. Only aggregate/reusable workflow structure is modeled; employee-specific facts remain restricted.

claims.claim: Of 33 individual-warning artifacts reviewed, 24 use a free-form 'To: Personnel File' memo pattern, 7 use the standardized Employee Warning Notice, and 2 use other narrative formats.

evidence.note: Counts describe document formats only; no employee-level facts are generalized.

claims.claim: Human Resources/EEO-role participation or authorship is visible in 25 of the 33 individual-warning artifacts, indicating HR commonly participated in or documented historical corrective-action meetings.

evidence.note: Role-level participation only; employee identities excluded.

claims.claim: Free-form personnel-file memos commonly record the date/time, people present, issue discussed, management/HR explanation, employee response or understanding, and the HR/manager author or signer.

The historical corpus shows counseling/cautioning could precede or coexist with formal numbered warnings, suspension, final warning and termination references; documentation style was not limited to a single standardized form.

evidence.note: This describes the range of documentation mechanisms, not the appropriate action for any case.

trigger: Performance, conduct, attendance or other employee issue is discussed/documented.
prerequisites: Facts of the issue are available.
Applicable policy/version is identified where possible.
steps: Document the date/time and issue prompting counseling or corrective action.
Discuss the concern, expectations and applicable policy/procedure with the employee.
Document corrective expectations or escalation consequences when applicable.
Use the standardized warning form when the formal-warning workflow requires it; otherwise historical practice sometimes used a personnel-file memo.
File the resulting disciplinary/counseling record in the appropriate restricted personnel record.
decisions: Whether informal counseling/memo documentation or a formal warning form is appropriate.
Whether escalation to a higher warning/suspension/termination review is warranted.
Which management/HR approvals or signatures are required.
exceptions: Historical documents show multiple formats; a free-form memo does not by itself indicate a lower or higher disciplinary level.
controls: Do not generalize one employee case into a universal policy.
Preserve participant/date/action provenance for each restricted case.
Keep disciplinary narratives and employee identities outside the generalized knowledge corpus.
Current approval/signature requirements must be validated before automating action decisions.
unresolved_questions: What current criteria determine whether HR documents an issue as informal counseling, a personnel-file memo, a formal warning, a performance plan, suspension or termination action?
Which disciplinary records belong in the personnel file versus a separate investigation/incident file?
What current signature/acknowledgment and employee-response procedures apply?
automation_candidates: Generate a structured restricted disciplinary case record from either a warning form or counseling memo while preserving the original source.
Detect repeated issues/prior related actions for reviewer context without automatically choosing discipline.
Require explicit human approval before any suspension, termination or other consequential action is generated.

provenance.notes: Only aggregate document structure and workflow patterns were generalized.
